evidenceAudit.scope: Women with a cervix: who to screen, which test and interval, when to stop, and how abnormal results are followed up in colposcopy. Verified against the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (Pap smear, grade A), the USPSTF 2018 recommendation and the NHS Cervical Screening Programme colposcopy management guidance.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi national cervical screening programme recall system not checked

pathophysiology.summary: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) causes cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), which can progress over years to invasive cancer. Screening detects hrHPV and precancer so it can be treated before cancer develops.
keyMechanisms: Most hrHPV infections clear; persistent infection drives CIN2/3 and, rarely, cancer.
Cytology detects abnormal cells; hrHPV testing is more sensitive and allows longer intervals (NHS CSP).
Excision of the transformation zone removes precancer; test of cure confirms clearance (NHS CSP).

symptoms: Symptoms needing investigation rather than screening: post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding, persistent unexplained discharge (NHS CSP section 2.5).
physicalSigns: Speculum examination; visible cervical lesion needs referral.
redFlags: Visible cervical lesion or abnormal bleeding — refer, do not rely on screening

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Discharge, contact bleeding — test for infection.
Benign; confirm screening is up to date.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Colposcopy per result; high grade always referred.

clinicalManagement.title: Who and how often
actions: PHA 2023 / USPSTF: age 21–29 cytology every 3 years; age 30–65 cytology every 3 years, or hrHPV alone or co-testing every 5 years.
Do not screen under 21, after hysterectomy with cervix removed (no CIN2+ history), or over 65 with adequate prior screening (USPSTF).

clinicalManagement.title: Act on results
actions: Abnormal cytology or persistent hrHPV: colposcopy referral (NHS CSP).
Inadequate cytology: repeat no sooner than 3 months (NHS CSP 3, section 1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Colposcopy
actions: Record hrHPV result, cytology grade, transformation zone type and biopsy sites (NHS CSP 3, section 1.3).
Excise when high-grade change is extensive or invasion is suspected (NHS CSP 3, section 1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Test of cure
actions: CGIN completely excised: test of cure at 6 months; if hrHPV negative, repeat 12 months later; both negative → recall in 3 years (NHS CSP 3, section 3.3).
hrHPV positive with abnormal cytology at test of cure → back to colposcopy.

learningObjectives: Screen for cervical precancer and ensure abnormal results are followed up.

pitfalls: Screening a woman with post-coital bleeding instead of examining her.
Screening after total hysterectomy without indication.
Losing patients to follow-up after abnormal results.

patientEducation: Screening prevents cancer by finding changes early.
HPV is common; a positive test does not mean cancer.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Follow recall intervals by test type; after treatment follow test-of-cure timings (NHS CSP).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Cytology every 3 years, or hrHPV ± cytology every 5 years
Over 65 with adequate prior screening; after hysterectomy without CIN2+ history
